correctness.rationale: Define distinct output shadow D(w) by four deletions. Verify ten orbits under alphabet relabeling and reversal, totaling all 81 inputs, with exact rational inequality sum_{y in D(w)}lambda(y)+mu(w)>=1. Output weights sum to 75/8, input slacks to 21/8, giving |C|<=171/8<22. A listed 21-word code gives exactly two distinct source words for every one of the 27 outputs. Its three conflict-shadow pairs have a triangle, proving the indicated nondecomposability. The embedded verifier reproduces all rational and finite checks without solver dependence.

originality.rationale: The four-coordinate ternary two-list deletion incidence optimum is not the uniquely decodable capacity, binary list capacity, or a deletion-covering number. The independently derived rational certificate and 21-word, two-fold-exact witness provide the exact missing finite invariant; relevant unindexed tables remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The finite optimum determines a natural, previously uncalibrated fixed-list deletion capacity at the smallest nontrivial ternary scale: the list-two size is 21, strictly less than twice the known uniquely decodable maximum 11. An explicit perfect twofold received-word cover attains the bound despite having a nonbipartite conflict triangle, showing that optimal list decoding is not merely partitioned unique decoding. The fractional upper certificate makes the result an exact structural benchmark, not a routine sample count.
